name: Example: Finding the Indefinite Integral of an Exponential-Trigonometric Expression Using Integration by Parts
worked_solution:
To use integration by parts, let's suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x=-\operatorname{cos}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =\int {e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{x}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)({e}^{x})\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\int {e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x+J.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we can use integration by parts to evaluate

$$
J = \int e^{x}\cos{x}\,\textrm{d}x.
$$

To do this, let's suppose that

$$
\begin{aligned}u={e}^{x}\, & ⇒\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x}\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\, & ⇒\,v=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the integration by parts formula once more, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}J & =\int {e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{x}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)-\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡x)({e}^{x})\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\int {e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-I.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this back into our equation for $I,$ we can subsequently solve for $I.$ We remember to add a constant of integration $C$ at the end.

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x+J \\ I & =-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x+{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x-I \\ 2I & =-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡x+{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ I & =\frac{{e}^{x}}{2}(\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{cos}⁡x)+C\end{aligned}
$$
